name: GitHub
headline: Easy: no review on either path. Waits depend on each customer's org owner installing or approving it.

firstTest.text: About 2 minutes: register my own OAuth app, generate a secret, and sign in.

production.text: Same day, no GitHub review. Your users' org owners must install a GitHub App, or approve an OAuth app if restrictions are on.

approvalWait.text: None. Registering showed 'Application created successfully' and the client ID at once. Only an optional Marketplace listing gets reviewed.

whoCanRegister.text: Any GitHub account can register an app. Pick 'Any account' as the install option. Paid plans need an org-owned app from a verified org.

testMode.text: No sandbox, no user caps. Both app types expire tokens by default: my test got an 8-hour access token and a 182-day refresh token.

actions.label: Read the user's profile
actions.scope: read:user (OAuth app) or Account permissions: read-only (GitHub App)

actions.label: Read code and issues in private repos
actions.scope: repo (OAuth app) or Contents / Issues: read-only (GitHub App)
actions.review: None from GitHub. In an org with app restrictions, an owner must approve an OAuth app. A GitHub App needs an owner install.
actions.timeToLive: same day, plus the org owner's wait

actions.label: Create issues and pull requests
actions.scope: repo (OAuth app) or Issues / Pull requests: read & write (GitHub App)
actions.review: None from GitHub. Same org rules as above.
actions.timeToLive: same day, plus the org owner's wait

actions.label: Read org and team membership
actions.scope: read:org (OAuth app) or Organization members: read-only (GitHub App)
actions.timeToLive: same day, plus the org owner's wait

actions.label: Edit GitHub Actions workflow files
actions.scope: workflow (OAuth app) or Workflows: read & write (GitHub App)
actions.review: None from GitHub. Ask for it only if your agent really edits workflows.

steps.title: Choose a GitHub App
steps.detail: Pick a GitHub App unless you need enterprise-level resources, which apps can't yet access. GitHub prefers apps for their fine-grained permissions, short-lived tokens and freedom from org OAuth restrictions.

steps.title: Register the app
steps.detail: Go to Settings > Developer settings > GitHub Apps > New GitHub App. Fill in the name and homepage URL (a repo URL works), and add up to 10 callback URLs.

steps.title: Set permissions
steps.detail: Grant the minimum each feature needs: Read-only, Read & write, or No access. Your choices also decide which webhook events you can subscribe to.

steps.title: Keep token expiry on
steps.detail: Leave 'Expire user authorization tokens' selected, as GitHub strongly recommends. User tokens then last 8 hours, with a refresh token valid for 6 months.

steps.title: Allow installs from any account
steps.detail: Set 'Where can this be installed' to 'Any account' so your users' accounts and orgs can install it. Optionally tick 'Request user authorization (OAuth) during installation' to merge install and sign-in.

steps.title: Build the sign-in flow
steps.detail: Send users to GitHub's authorize page with a state value and the usual extra security check. Swap the code for tokens, store both, and refresh before the 8 hours end.

steps.title: Test with a real org
steps.detail: Install the app on an org you own, using a member account that isn't an owner. Check that the request to the owner appears and the owner can approve it.

steps.title: Tell customers what owners do
steps.detail: Org owners install the app. Repo admins can install it only if it asks for no org permissions and no Repository administration. Non-owners send a request to the owner.

steps.title: List on Marketplace (optional)
steps.detail: Not required. Do it only for discovery or paid plans, which need a verified org and financial onboarding.

blockers.title: Your customer's org owner hasn't installed or approved the app
blockers.fix: For a GitHub App, a non-owner who picks the org sends the owner a request. For an OAuth app, the owner approves it under third-party application access; add a 'send this link to your admin' screen.

blockers.title: New orgs block OAuth apps by default
blockers.fix: Restrictions turn on automatically for new orgs, so members can't authorize an OAuth app for org data until an owner approves it. A GitHub App avoids this policy, per GitHub's comparison page.

blockers.title: Your users' tokens expire after 8 hours
blockers.fix: Refresh with the refresh token and save the new one each time. When the 182-day (about 6-month) refresh token expires, run sign-in again.

blockers.title: You need enterprise-level resources
blockers.fix: A GitHub App can't yet get permissions against an enterprise. Use an OAuth app for those calls.

blockers.title: Users trim permissions after signing in (OAuth app)
blockers.fix: Users can edit granted scopes after the flow. Check what was actually granted on every call, and handle reduced access.

blockers.title: Users hesitate at a brand-new app
blockers.fix: GitHub's consent screen shows 'Created less than a day ago' and 'Fewer than 10 GitHub users'. Create the app well before launch, and add a logo and description.

agentCan: Write the web and device sign-in code, with state and the extra security checks
Map each agent action to the smallest permission or scope
Add token refresh and secure storage
Draft the 'ask your org owner' screen and copy
Check granted permissions on each call and fall back gracefully
youDo: Sign in to GitHub and register the app
Keep the client secret and private key safe
Test with a real org where you are not an owner
Your customers' org owners install or approve the app
Accept the Marketplace Developer Agreement if you list

drafts.title: GitHub App description
drafts.body: [Product] lets your AI assistant work in your GitHub repos. It reads issues and code you choose, and can open issues and pull requests when you ask. It only gets the access you grant on the install screen.

drafts.title: Message for an org owner
drafts.body: Hi, we'd like to connect [Product] to our GitHub org. It asks for read access to [Contents, Issues] and write access to [Pull requests]. You can pick which repositories it sees. Please review and install it here: [install link].

drafts.title: Permissions explainer for your connect screen
drafts.body: We ask for the smallest set we need: read repository contents and issues, and write pull requests. We never see repos you don't share. You can remove access any time in GitHub settings.
